name: bounded collective fixed-normal clearance with exact opposite-row pruning
activation: Pipeline9ClearanceProjectionSolver uses CollectiveClearanceSolver for its ordinary candidate construction
replacement: Retain native geometry, junction/endpoint locks, near-pair/pad preparation and finalization. Replace 256 projection sweeps with finite separating-normal families and jointly coupled x/y half-space feasibility.
physicalContract: Each selected unit normal constrains every endpoint pair (or both segment endpoints against every pad corner), proving separation for complete straight segments and the convex pad rectangle.
Native endpoint/junction/through-obstacle locks, route/layer/width/terminal metadata, board bounds and via colocation are retained.

Distinct drill sites receive owner-independent center separation including the caller hole diameter and hole-edge clearance, even for disjoint blind spans. A shared same-net physical site can remain shared.
The unchanged existing exact fixed-obstacle, new-via/pad and reference DRC publication guards remain authoritative. The candidate does not claim to be physically clean.
proofLimits: Normals include closest endpoint/segment contacts, both segment perpendiculars, rotated pad sides and axis choices. The finite set is still incomplete for arbitrary geometric motion.

Hildreth dual coordinate updates start from zero displacement and tend toward its Euclidean projection. Termination requires a fully checked feasible witness, not an optimality certificate. Bounds remain the native +/-0.25 per-axis box.

General nonconvergence, work/sweep exhaustion or numerical uncertainty is UNKNOWN. A selected choice can be rejected only by exact opposite finite rows whose bound sum is negative beyond 2*tolerance plus roundoff. The receiver independently rechecks that 2-row certificate; it applies only to current component/side choices, never the whole PCB.

Empty side domains remain explicit unresolved. Oversized/unknown components retain originals; newly encountered violations trigger a strengthened bounded solve or transaction rollback. Native projection is never a fallback.
Native quadratic preparation remains. Pinned private preparation fields are shape-checked, not a public upstream API. Existing exact physical/reference publication guards are unchanged.
Dynamic scheduler reserves owned native allowance and a finite remaining model bound without increasing physical, branch, row-check or separation-round budgets.

Canonical row keys use exact round-trip finite coefficients, never rounded vector hashing. Hash lookup proposes a pair; sorted coefficient identity and finite negative bound sum are independently checked. No Farkas or general convex infeasibility inference is implemented.

counterMeaning.preparedPairCount: Native setup pair examinations retained as actual work.
counterMeaning.constraintChecks: Sum of executed dual row updates, residual-row checks and final clamped-coordinate witness checks across all assignments and rounds.
counterMeaning.rowUpdates: Executed Hildreth nonnegative dual coordinate updates, including zero updates.
counterMeaning.residualChecks: Executed full current-point half-space residual checks.
counterMeaning.witnessChecks: Final full half-space validation after native-coordinate rounding/clamping.
counterMeaning.unknownChoiceAssignments: Nonconverged finite side assignments; never proven infeasible.
counterMeaning.residualBranches: Generated finite side choices suggested by residuals; no hard clauses.
counterMeaning.generatedNormalChoices: All constructed finite separating directions across repeated model rounds.
counterMeaning.branchVariableInstances: Sum of variable slots in executed assignments, not unique vertices or allocated bytes.
counterMeaning.maxBranchVariables: Largest assignment variable count; a gauge, not additive work.
counterMeaning.maxBranchRows: Largest assignment row count; a gauge, not additive work.
counterMeaning.selectedObliqueRows: Executed assignment rows involving both x and y, including repeated choices.
counterMeaning.changedFamilyChoices: Sum of side choices differing from the first ranked choice over executed assignments.
counterMeaning.movedVertices: Accepted component movement events across rounds, including later discarded rounds; not unique final vertices.
counterMeaning.generatedConstraintEdges: Constructed alternative half-space rows, including unselected alternatives.
counterMeaning.unknownComponents: Components retaining original coordinates, not globally infeasible components.
counterMeaning.rolledBackUncertainCandidate: Entire candidate restored after new violations remain at model/round cap.
counterMeaning.preprocessingRows: Executed canonical row preprocessing before numerical projection. Separate from the 2 million update/residual/witness cap.
counterMeaning.hashProbes: Actual canonical/opposite map lookups. Keys use exact finite round-trip coefficients.
counterMeaning.canonicalizedTerms: Term entries copied/canonicalized for row-key construction.
counterMeaning.hashKeyCharacters: Characters in constructed key strings, not actual retained bytes or CPU time.
counterMeaning.exactRowChecks: Calls to the exact two-row verifier, including receiver rechecks and benign proposed pairs.
counterMeaning.proofTermReads: Term entries read by independent exact-certificate checking.
counterMeaning.exactTermComparisons: Paired coefficient comparisons during certificate checking.
counterMeaning.certificateRechecks: Receiver verifies returned certificate against current selected rows before using its families.
counterMeaning.certifiedChoiceContradictions: Current selected side assignments rejected by a checked exact two-row proof.
counterMeaning.certifiedFamilyReferences: Family references in accepted two-row certificates, not unique persistent global clauses.
counterMeaning.certifiedBranchesGenerated: Finite alternative choices that change at least one certified family.
counterMeaning.boundedHardContradictions: Checked pair uses only hard rows with no side family; scoped to current bounded model and returns unresolved component, not PCB infeasibility.
